1. India has the second largest population and
is the largest democracy in the world.
2. There is confluence of many religions, languages
and cultures in India. People have been living
in harmony for many centuries.
3. India is a secular state and therefore,
communali sm is contrary to the spirit of
the Indian Constitution. However, communal
tensions and conflicts emerge in a society
when a group of communal-m inded people
act against the people belonging to the other
religious groups.
4. Communali sm means ~xcessive love for one's.
religion and excessive hatred for the other
religions. They look upon every issue from
communal perspective and thereby shatter
social harmony.
5. The right to freedom of religion enables the
religious minorities to practise their religion.
6. The National Minorities· Commission was set
up by the constitution to protect' the interests
of the religious minorities as well as to look
after their welfare and development.
7. Casteism is an outcome of the caste-based
social structure of India. There were four
Varnas in ancient India, namely Brahmin,
Kshatriya. Vaishya and Shudra. These later
evolved into hundreds of localized Jatts - castes.
There was segretation in matter of residence.
There were caste-based occupations . Some
castes were getting low income, so they
remained economically poor.
